text: Part four, the finale. Boston, nineteen ninety. After midnight, two police officers knock at a museum door. They say they're answering a call. The guard lets them in. But they weren't police. They handcuffed the guards, and tied them up in the basement. Then they took their time. Eighty-one minutes later, they were gone, with thirteen works of art. A Vermeer. Rembrandt's only seascape. Worth up to five hundred million dollars. Today, the empty frames still hang on the walls. There's a ten-million-dollar reward. No one has ever been charged, and the art has never been found. Which heist should we build next? Tell us in the comments.
